rows.title: blonde hedgehog
rows.evidence: The source names blonde hedgehogs and says they are extremely rare except on North Ronaldsay and Alderney.
rows.summary: The European hedgehog (Erinaceus europaeus), also known as the West European hedgehog, Western European hedgehog or common hedgehog, is a hedgehog species native to Europe from Iberia and Italy northwards into Scandinavia and westwards into Ireland. They are extremely rare, except on North Ronaldsay and the Channel Island of Alderney, where around 25% of the population is thought to be blonde.

rows.title: Dactylorhiza francis-drucei var. ebudensis
rows.evidence: The article gives var. ebudensis the range North Uist, and gives the other accepted taxa wider ranges.
rows.summary: Dactylorhiza francis-drucei is a species of terrestrial orchid native to Great Britain and Ireland. Dactylorhiza francis-drucei var. ebudensis (Wief. ex R.M.Bateman & Denholm) R.M.Bateman & Denholm – North Uist.

rows.title: Alpine rock-cress
rows.evidence: The article says that in the British Isles Arabis alpina is only known from the Cuillin Ridge of the Isle of Skye.
rows.summary: Arabis alpina, the Alpine rock-cress, is a flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae, native to mountainous areas of Europe, North and East Africa, Central and Eastern Asia and parts of North America. In the British Isles, it is only known to occur in a few locations in the Cuillin Ridge of the Isle of Skye.

rows.title: Edwardsia delapiae
rows.evidence: The article says the anemone is currently only known from Valentia harbour, and the word Valentia is linked to the Valentia Island article.
rows.summary: Edwardsia delapiae is a species of sea anemone which is currently only known from its type locality in south-western Ireland. This species is currently only known from Valentia harbour, County Kerry, Ireland.

rows.title: Atlantic puffin
rows.evidence: The Skomer article says the Atlantic puffin colony is the largest in southern Britain.
rows.summary: Skomer (Welsh: Ynys Sgomer) or Skomer Island is an island off the coast of Pembrokeshire, in the community of Marloes and St Brides in west Wales. The Atlantic puffin colony is the largest in southern Britain.

rows.title: Pied avocet
rows.evidence: The Havergate Island article says the UK's largest breeding population of pied avocets can be found there. The atlas record is the only Havergate island, and its area matches the island described.
rows.summary: Havergate Island is an island in the civil parish of Orford, in the East Suffolk district, in the county of Suffolk, England. It is a marshy nature reserve run by the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) and is known for its population of pied avocets and terns. The UK's largest breeding population of pied avocets and Suffolk's only breeding Sandwich terns can be found there.

rows.title: Red squirrel
rows.evidence: The red squirrel article calls the Isle of Wight the largest haven in England.
rows.summary: Although not thought to be under any threat worldwide, the red squirrel has nevertheless drastically reduced in number in the United Kingdom; especially after the eastern grey squirrel was introduced from North America in the 1870s. Fewer than 140,000 individuals are thought to be left in 2013; approximately 85% of which are in Scotland, with the Isle of Wight being the largest haven in England.

rows.title: Roccella fuciformis
rows.evidence: The Annet article calls the island the British stronghold for the lichen Roccella fuciformis.
rows.summary: Annet is the ″British stronghold″ for the lichen Roccella fuciformis.

rows.title: wall lizard
rows.evidence: The Jersey article says Jersey is the only native habitat in the British Isles for the wall lizard.
rows.summary: All are protected species, with Jersey being the only native habitat in the British Isles for the green lizard, wall lizard, spiny toad and agile frog.

rows.title: spiny toad
rows.evidence: The Jersey article says Jersey is the only native habitat in the British Isles for the spiny toad.
rows.summary: All are protected species, with Jersey being the only native habitat in the British Isles for the green lizard, wall lizard, spiny toad and agile frog.

rows.title: agile frog
rows.evidence: The Jersey article says Jersey is the only native habitat in the British Isles for the agile frog.
rows.summary: All are protected species, with Jersey being the only native habitat in the British Isles for the green lizard, wall lizard, spiny toad and agile frog.

rows.title: Jersey fern
rows.evidence: The article calls Anogramma leptophylla Jersey fern and says the only place it occurs in the British Isles is Jersey.
rows.summary: Anogramma leptophylla, sometimes called Jersey fern, is a species of fern in the family Pteridaceae. The only place in the British Isles in which it occurs is the island of Jersey in the Channel Islands.

rows.title: Loose Flowered orchid
rows.evidence: The article says that in the United Kingdom the orchid is represented only on the Channel Islands, and that in Guernsey it is called Loose Flowered orchid.
rows.summary: Anacamptis laxiflora (lax-flowered orchid, loose-flowered orchid, or green-winged meadow orchid) is a species of orchid. A. laxiflora is common in Normandy and Brittany (France), but in the United Kingdom it is represented only on the Channel Islands, where in Jersey it is called Jersey orchid and in Guernsey it is called Loose Flowered orchid.

rows.title: Isle of Man cabbage
rows.evidence: The article says the plant grows around the coasts of the Isle of Man and was named because it was once abundant there. A second atlas record, wd-Q27508141, is the same island; the curated id is the one already used for wildlife there.
rows.summary: Coincya monensis subsp. monensis, the Isle of Man cabbage, is a species of plant in the family Brassicaceae that is found in coastal habitats on the west of the island of Great Britain (from north Devon to Kintyre) and around the coasts of the Isle of Man. The species was once abundant on the Isle of Man, hence its name, however, for an unknown reason its population has collapsed to only a few individual and isolated plants.

rows.title: South Stack fleawort
rows.evidence: The article says the fleawort is endemic to Holyhead Island. The Holy Island (Anglesey) article says that island's alternative English name is Holyhead Island, which matches this atlas record and not the other Holy Islands.
rows.summary: Tephroseris integrifolia subsp. maritima, also known as the spathulate fleawort or South Stack fleawort, is endemic to Holyhead Island, occurring only around South Stack. It is a subspecies of the field fleawort Tephroseris integrifolia.

rows.title: Hebridean wren
rows.evidence: The subspecies hebridensis is placed on the Outer Hebrides.
rows.summary: In Scotland, in addition to the typical bird N. t. indigenus widespread in Britain and Ireland, there are four distinct insular subspecies; one, N. t. hirtensis, is confined to the island of St Kilda; another, N. t. zetlandicus, to Shetland; the third, N. t. fridariensis, to Fair Isle; and the fourth, N. t. hebridensis, to the Outer Hebrides.
rows.reject_reason: The article places the Hebridean wren on the Outer Hebrides as a group. No sentence names one island.

rows.title: Scottish primrose
rows.evidence: The range is the north coast of mainland Scotland and the Orkney Islands.
rows.summary: Primula scotica is endemic to northern Scotland where it is found along the northern, Pentland Firth, coast of the mainland in the Highland in the former counties of Caithness and Sutherland and on the other side of the Pentland Firth in the Orkney Islands.
rows.reject_reason: The range is the northern mainland coast and the Orkney Islands together. No one Orkney island is named as the stronghold.

rows.title: slender Scotch burnet
rows.source_title: List of moths of Great Britain (Zygaenidae)
rows.evidence: The page lists Zygaena loti scotica on the islands of Mull and Ulva.
rows.summary: Zygaena loti scotica — islands of Mull & Ulva (Red Data Book).
rows.reject_reason: The only wording is a checklist line. The same page was already judged not to tie this moth to Mull, and it does not contain a sentence that makes Ulva the stronghold.

rows.title: Manx shearwater
rows.evidence: The sentence that calls Skokholm home to the third-largest Manx shearwater colony also gives a world-population share and other colony counts.
rows.reject_reason: The sentence that calls Skokholm the third-largest Manx shearwater colony also gives a world-population share and nest counts, so it cannot be stored.

rows.title: Dwarf pansy
rows.evidence: The sentence that places the dwarf pansy on Bryher also gives a count and a month.
rows.reject_reason: The sentence that places the dwarf pansy on Bryher says thousands can be found in May, which is a count and advice on when to see it.

rows.title: Guernsey lily
rows.evidence: The article says the plant is associated with Guernsey by name and does not originate there.
rows.summary: Nerine sarniensis, commonly known as Guernsey lily or Raquel is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae. It is particularly associated with the island of Guernsey, as reflected in both its Latin and common names (sarniensis means "from Guernsey"), though it does not originate there, nor is it a true lily. It is native to the Northern and Western Cape Provinces of South Africa.
rows.reject_reason: It is a South African plant. The article says it does not originate on Guernsey and does not say it grows wild there.

rows.title: Kerry slug
rows.evidence: The article places the slug in south-western Ireland and at Caragh Lake.
rows.summary: Although the distribution of this slug species includes south-western Ireland—including County Kerry—the species is more widespread in north-western Spain and central-to-northern Portugal.
rows.reject_reason: The article does not name one atlas island as the stronghold.

rows.title: great skua
rows.evidence: The great skua article does not name Foula.
rows.reject_reason: No sentence calls Foula the stronghold of the great skua.

rows.title: Leach's storm petrel
rows.evidence: North Rona is called an important breeding locality for Leach's storm petrel.
rows.summary: These include the European storm-petrel and the larger Leach's storm-petrel, for which North Rona is an important breeding locality.
rows.reject_reason: An important breeding locality is not a principal stronghold.
